Hello @poojaranjan, thanks for make this happen.

**We want to present EIP Lab in this call**: 

We are: @ariutokintumi @0xoucan

EIP Lab is a free and open-source solution for testing and deploying EIP on any EVM without client modifications, forks, or testnet releases.

[Alpha version](https://eiplabv1.vercel.app/lab)
[Repo](https://github.com/EVVM-org/eip-lab)
[X Post announcement with more info](https://x.com/RollAMate/status/2064052557169709197)

_Note: No AI credits are provided; use your API key or, better yet, deploy the solution locally for greater control.._

I want to add some items to the agenda: (doing a brain dump here so I can later ref to these points)

Moving EIP to Review. Moving Glamsterdam Meta EIP to Review is challenging because all EIPs it refer seems to require by EIP Walidator that all those referenced are also in Review or higher. I am not sure if it is correct, there could be circumstances (even for Final EIPs) where we would want to link to Draft/Stagnant/Withdrawn EIPs for historical purposes, see [this comment](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11855#issuecomment-4871769609). Also see [this](https://github.com/ethereum/eipw/issues/95) EIPW issue.

Other:

## Eth-bot merging related
1. The merge policy of eth-bot. It squashes all commits, but it does not keep co-authorship of the commits made. If an EIP is authored by multiple users (so multi-commits by multiple users, or a single commit by multiple users (actually not sure what eth-bot does in this case)). I also feel that by editorial reviews we do, the suggestions we make (even if it is a small typo one) should be added as co-author. The main reason for this is direct accountability, if an author applies one of our suggestions, then in the commit (even if this is adding a full EIP) it will "look" like this is "their" doing. Especially if we do things "wrong" (for instance suggesting proceeding to preceeding, while the former was correct) this should then show up in `git blame`. If a commit is then authored by multiple authors we can go back (to the un-squashed PR) to figure out "who to blame" here, which directly is related to the next point:
2. eth-bot should include the PR number of the (squashed) commit(s). In some cases it seems that GitHub finds the original PR, but in most cases not. This is again for keeping history (even though this will not be part of the git history, but will be part of the history on GitHub) and is helpful to quickly figure out where something was changed instead of figuring this out with extra `git` commands.

## EIPW rules

3. EIPW should enforce: 
- EIPs/ERCs on first reference MUST be have an URL link
- RFCs on first reference MUST have an RFC link (RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 are used in most (new) EIPs I have seen and most of them do not have URLs.
- Copyright waiver enforcement. We require this line per EIP-1, we should enforce this by the bot to prevent accidentally merging EIPs with no copyright or with an incomplete copyright.

## ERC-related Solidity rules

4. External libaries in Solidity code

Getting a bit more freshed up on Solidity now with these ERCs. One thing I noticed in a PR:

`import { IAllowanceTransfer, IPermit2 } from "@permit2/interfaces/IPermit2.sol";` 

in the Reference Implementation section implementation. I am not sure if other ERCs do this but I do not think we should allow these external libraries to be used, especially if it is not clear what this `@permit2` references to. It's a bit of a grey area for me since this is in the Reference Implementation section, but: using external libraries assumes that their exports if it changes is fully backward-compatible. In the future it could also be unknown what is meant, if such external library is currently not standard and/or these entities cease to exist.

## If time allows (misc)

5. Enforcing RFC 2119 keywords only in Specification section.
- I am getting convinced that [this](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/e0554048836ac2b66dc9b90c324473a9f0b5dc06/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L15) rule 

> Don't use [RFC 2119](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2119.html) keywords (all-caps SHOULD/MUST/etc.) outside of the specification section.

Is one we should (MUST 😜 ) enforce. Used elsewhere they could accidentally be a specification which is out-of-place. If capitalized letters are used to emphasize something, then people can also use markdown markup like **bold**.

The bot rule will be rather complex to write correctly though, I assume.

6. Change default branch to `main` to the  EIPs, ERCs and RIPs repositories.

Can we also add this PR to the agenda? https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11845

@danceratopz is an (awesome 😄 ) member of the STEEL team so I can vouch for these URLs to be removed, as these URLs now have moved to the `execution-specs` repository. Also seems we added it twice to EIP-1 😅 . We should maybe setup a date to go over EIP-1 together to polish it up and to verify if it all is still correct. I think we should also add RFC 2119 keywords in it.
